You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",
 "summary": "<3-5 sentences: what happened or is expected, why, how sure>",
 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

  "headline": "The ACCELERATE trial of evacetrapib was stopped for futility in ~12,092 high-risk vascular patients, confirming that CETP inhibition does not reduce cardiovascular events despite large HDL-C increases.",
  "summary": "The ACCELERATE trial randomized 12,092–12,095 patients with high-risk vascular disease to evacetrapib 130 mg or placebo on background statin therapy. The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina, with 1,670 planned events. The independent data monitoring committee stopped the trial early on October 12, 2015, for insufficient efficacy with no safety signal. Evacetrapib produced massive HDL-C elevations (+129% within-arm, +103% placebo-adjusted) and modest LDL-C lowering (~‑15% placebo-adjusted), but the calculator predicted only a 37% probability of success (expected HR 0.923) based on the LDL-C effect, yielding 37% power (MDE HR 0.872 for 80% power). Human genetics available at trial launch showed a CETP association score of 0.736 but zero supporting studies before the 2015 cutoff, indicating HDL-C is not a causal mediator for coronary disease.
